stem.en: Why does a river deposit a delta at its mouth?

text.en: The sea pushes extra sand up the river to its source.

feedback.en: The sediment of a delta comes down the river from upstream.

text.en: The water slows down and cannot carry its load.

feedback.en: Right. Slow water drops its sediment.

text.en: The river speeds up and throws its load forward.

feedback.en: The river slows at the mouth. It does not speed up.

text.en: The river bed turns to hard rock near the sea.

feedback.en: A delta is made of soft sediment that the river carried and dropped.

explanation.en: When a river enters still water it slows and can no longer carry its load. Sediment settles, blocks the way, and the river splits into distributaries around new islands and bars.

hints.en: What happens to the speed of the river when it enters the sea?
